plan: [I have a private value of $9. In a sealed-bid second-price auction, bidding my true value is a dominant strategy: I win when the second-highest bid is below $9 and then pay that price, yielding nonnegative surplus. Overbidding can risk paying more than my value if others bid high. With one round and independent draws, truthful bidding maximizes expected profit.]

[This is a single-round sealed-bid second-price (Vickrey) auction. Truthful bidding is a weakly dominant strategy: bid your private value. There is no prior history to learn from. Bidding above risks paying >9 if others bid between 9 and your inflated bid; bidding below can miss profitable wins. I will bid my true value of $9.00 to maximize expected payoff.]

[ In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true private value is a weakly dominant strategy. With value $34 and independent draws, bidding 34 maximizes expected payoff and avoids overpaying. No prior history; one round. ]
